newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada public, private investment rises in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Canada public, private investment rises in 1997.

text.p: Statistics Canada said on Wednesday that revised investment intentions for the public and private sector in 1997 rose to C$146.6 billion, an 11.6 percent rise from actual investment in 1996.
StatsCan said business and government planned to invest a record C$110.9 billion in plants and equipment in 1997, an 11 percent increase from 1996.
This is the fourth consecutive gain and the largest annual increase in investment since 1993, Statistics Canada said.
This latest survey shows much stronger overall investment for 1997 with an increase of C$6.6 billion from what was originally planned this year, StatsCan said.
The agency said that buoyed by solid gains in production, accompanied by healthy profits and rising rates of capacity use, companies are spending in plants and equipment at record levels.
StatsCan said the growth is evident in many sectors of the economy, especially the service-producing industries, which account for 54 percent of the overall 11.6 percent increase.
(For more information contact Gilbert Paquette at 613-951-9818 at Statistics Canada)
